newsitem.title: USA: Golfer Greg Norman to be Boeing "ambassador".
newsitem.headline: Golfer Greg Norman to be Boeing "ambassador".

text.p: Golf star Greg Norman said on Monday he has signed a seven-year, multimillion-dollar deal to be an "ambassador" for Boeing Co. and especially its new line of business jets.
Norman also announced an agreement to buy one of the first next-generation 737 jets specially outfitted for business use.
A Boeing spokeswoman said Norman, ranked the world's No. 1 golfer, was the first celebrity endorser for the company in recent memory and perhaps ever.

"This is a new idea and obviously we're very happy to have the association with Greg Norman," said Boeing's Barbara Murphy. She said Norman could appear in advertising, at marketing events or speaking engagements on Boeing's behalf.
Norman's efforts at first will be directed at promoting the Boeing Business Jet, a version of the twin-engine 737 configured for business use and outfitted to customer specifications.

Norman said he decided to trade in his Gulfstream in favor of a Boeing mainly because the much larger 737 would allow more of his employees to work or sleep on long trips to the Far East or between Australia and his home in south Florida.

Norman said he logged some 275,000 miles (442,600 km) of air travel last year getting to golf tournaments and maintaining his far-flung Great White Shark Enterprises Inc., which has interests in golf course design, apparel manufacturing, a sod farm and a restaurant business.

Boeing officials said Norman paid the list price of slightly more than $30 million for his jet, which will be delivered in late 1998. It typically costs another $6 million to furnish and paint a 737 to business specifications.
